# Package Manager Integration

How dependency graph tools interact with pip, poetry, uv, conda, and
their respective file formats.

## Resolver Algorithms

| Manager | Algorithm | Key Characteristic |
|---------|-----------|-------------------|
| uv | PubGrub (pubgrub-rs) | Forking resolver for platform-specific deps [18] |
| Poetry | PubGrub (mixology) | Full tree consideration [37] |
| pip | Backtracking (resolvelib) | Since 20.3; can be slow on complex graphs [19] |
| conda | SAT (libmamba/libsolv) | 50-80% faster than classic solver [24] |

**uv** uses pubgrub-rs, a Rust implementation of the PubGrub incremental
version solver [18]. The key performance optimization: metadata loading is
the bottleneck, not computation itself — uv prefetches metadata in the
background and uses lockfile version preferences to minimize backtracking [18].

**Poetry** uses mixology, a Python PubGrub implementation [37]. Can be
slow when PyPI metadata is incomplete, requiring package downloads to
inspect dependencies [37].

**pip** introduced backtracking resolution in version 20.3 [19]. On complex
graphs, backtracking manifests as multiple downloads of the same package at
different versions [19].

**conda** adopted libmamba (built on libsolv from openSUSE) as the default
solver in version 23.10.0, achieving 50-80% run time improvement over the
classic pycosat-based solver [24].

## Performance Benchmarks

Using Sentry's dependency set (via Python Package Manager Shootout) [27]:

| Operation | uv | Poetry | pip-tools |
|-----------|-------|--------|-----------|
| Cold lock install | ~3s | ~11s | ~33s |
| Lock file generation | ~8s | ~22s | ~35s |

uv has ~75M monthly PyPI downloads, surpassing Poetry's 66M, and has
"overtaken pip as the primary installer in CI environments" [27].

## File Format Support

### Dependency Specification Files

| Format | Used By | Structured Groups | Lock Support |
|--------|---------|-------------------|-------------|
| pyproject.toml | uv, Poetry, PDM, Setuptools | Yes | Via separate lock file |
| requirements.txt | pip, pip-tools | No | Is the lock file |
| Pipfile / Pipfile.lock | Pipenv | Yes | Yes |
| environment.yml | conda | Yes | Via conda-lock |

### Lockfile Formats

| Format | Manager | Portability |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| uv.lock | uv | Universal (cross-platform/OS/arch/Python) [17] |
| poetry.lock | Poetry | Platform-specific by default |
| requirements.txt (pinned) | pip-tools | Platform-specific |
| pylock.toml (PEP 751) | Standard | Multi-environment [23] |

**PEP 751** (accepted March 31, 2025) standardizes `pylock.toml` as the
official Python lock file format [23]. TOML-based with consistent key
ordering, supporting multi-environment configurations via extras and
dependency groups [23]. Tool authors are expected to implement PEP 751
as an export format but may retain their own lockfiles [23].

## Tool Compatibility with Package Managers

| Tool | pip | Poetry | uv | PDM | Pipenv | conda |
|------|-----|--------|------|-----|--------|-------|
| pipdeptree | Yes | — | — | — | — | — |
| deptry | Yes [5] | Yes [5] | Yes [5] | Yes [5] | — | — |
| pip-audit | Yes [6] | — | — | — | — | — |
| uv audit | — | — | Yes [28] | — | — | — |
| Safety | Yes [13] | Yes | — | — | Yes | — |
| Trivy | Yes [14] | Yes [14] | Yes [14] | — | Yes [14] | SBOM only [14] |
| Snyk | Yes [16] | Yes [16] | — | — | Yes [16] | — |
| import-linter | Any (source analysis) [9] | | | | | |
| tach | Any (source analysis) [20] | | | | | |

Note: import-linter and tach analyze source imports, not installed packages,
so they work with any package manager.

## Dependency Pinning Trade-offs

Research shows pinning is "most likely to result in outdated dependencies" [52].
Survival analysis confirms pinning more likely to produce outdated deps than
floating version constraints [53]. Recommendation: use floating-patch
constraints (e.g., `>=1.2,<2`) for security/stability balance [53].

## Gaps and Limitations

- pipdeptree only works with installed packages (pip-based environments) [2]
- uv audit only works with uv-managed projects [28]
- No tool supports PEP 751 pylock.toml yet [23]
- conda environments are poorly supported by most graph tools [14]
- deptry requires virtual environment for metadata access [4]
- Trivy's pip support limited to `==` specifiers by default [14]
